mergeRequest.description:
## What does this MR do and why?

`LocalConfigDir` resolved through `git rev-parse --git-dir`, which in a linked worktree is `.git/worktrees/<name>`. Local config set in the main checkout was therefore invisible in every worktree, and each new worktree started empty and silently fell back to global.

This resolves through `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` instead, so one repository has one local config. Git shares `.git/config` the same way and makes per-worktree config opt-in, and these keys describe the repository rather than the checkout. Stacks were moved to the common dir for the same reason in `0a119c022`.

## References

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8568

Prior art in the same repository: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8355 moved stacks to the common dir. The per-worktree location came from https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/7872, which this keeps available as an existing-file override rather than the default.

## Differences

**Before:** in a linked worktree, `glab config get` read `.git/worktrees/<name>/glab-cli/config.yml` and saw none of the repository's config.

**After:** it reads `.git/glab-cli/config.yml`, the same file the main checkout writes.

A worktree that already carries its own file keeps using it, so a config written before this change still applies where it was written. A normal checkout is unaffected, because both flags resolve to the same directory, and a submodule keeps its own under `.git/modules/<name>`.

## Two details worth a reviewer's eye

`git` answers `--git-common-dir` with a relative, forward-slash path where it answers `--git-dir` with an absolute one, when run from a subdirectory:

```
$ cd a/b
$ git rev-parse --git-dir
C:/.../repo/.git
$ git rev-parse --git-common-dir
../../.git
```

The old code always went through `filepath.Rel`, which normalised separators. The relative branch now cleans the result to the platform separator, otherwise `Test_LocalConfigDir` fails on Windows with `../../.git` against `..\..\.git`.

`CheckPathExists` returns `info.IsDir()`, so it reports only directories. The backwards-compatible lookup uses `CheckFileExists` instead. My first attempt used the wrong one and the existing-file override silently never fired.

## How to set up and validate locally

End to end, which is the reproduction from the issue:

```shell
go build -o /tmp/glab ./cmd/glab
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/main && cd /tmp/repro/main
git init -q . && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init
/tmp/glab config set editor main-only-editor
git worktree add -q --detach ../wt && cd ../wt
/tmp/glab config get editor
```

```markdown
## MR acceptance checklist

- [x] Tests added, verified to fail without the fix
- [x] Reproduced end to end against binaries built from this branch and from `main`
- [x] Existing per-worktree files keep working
- [x] Packages that share `GitDir` pass unchanged
- [x] Conforms to the code review guidelines
```
